page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-standard-8 is a compute-focused virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor built on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core, supported by 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. The system is provisioned with 32.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware accelerators such as GPUs are not included, and the instance provides no bundled local NVMe storage or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating attached network storage for persistent filesystem operations.

Benchmark results reveal strong single-threaded performance, with stress-ng single-core execution scoring 2865.09 to place within the top 25th percentile. Multi-core compute falls within the middle 50th percentile, evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core score of 11559.23, a Geekbench multi-core rating of 6531.0, and a clang software compilation score of 7872.0. Large-block uncached memory throughput reaches 46.79 GB/s for reads and 32.75 GB/s for writes. In application benchmarks, the instance delivers 8.77 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and sustains 10.68 GB/s in static web serving throughput.

Given its combination of high single-core capability and balanced per-core memory capacity, c2d-standard-8 offers high utility for compile-heavy CI/CD pipelines, containerized application servers, and in-memory key-value databases. The primary architectural tradeoff is the absence of local storage, which directs I/O-intensive workloads to rely entirely on external networked storage volumes.

It provides 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores, 32.0 GB of memory (4.0 GB per vCPU), and 32 MB of L3 cache. The configuration excludes local storage and GPU acceleration, directing storage requirements toward network-attached volumes. In benchmark testing, the instance demonstrates strong single-core CPU throughput in the top 25th percentile, coupled with median-tier multi-threaded execution and memory bandwidth. The instance represents an efficient hardware balance for software compilation, CI/CD runners, high-traffic web backends, and distributed caching systems.
